fieldValues.title: Dissent is recorded on the decision it disagrees with
fieldValues.move: Whenever an agent dissents in operation (a reviewer's `decision <id>: dissent`, a reviewer's finding the builder accepts rather than fixes, a minority view in a multi-agent review), write it as a comment on the decision record, tagged dissent, with who, why and the PR it came from. A decision's revisit then reads its dissent first, and the session agenda shows how much dissent each decision carries. Start by observing: take a few multi-agent decision processes as they run and record their dissent by hand before automating it.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: It does not make agents dissent well, or at all: a reviewer prompted to agree will not. It does not decide what a revisit does with the dissent. A finding with no decision to attach to (a code choice in a PR) still has no home unless the PR names one.
fieldValues.falsifier: Over a few cycles the recorded dissent never changes a revisit, a ratification or a revisit trigger; or it is so frequent and so minor that nobody reads it.
source_ref: muDemocracy.org/reference/Delegation in historic small democracy.md (report-back element 5; the John Lewis published reply; Dedham's unrecorded votes)
fieldValues.return_when: Agent reviews are rare enough that the PR history is read anyway at every revisit.
